question: to the Commission Erik Kaliňák (NI) Subject:
EUR 150 billion for EU defence. How much of this will the Slovak defence industry actually receive?

Last year, the Council of the EU approved the SAFE instrument, with a maximum volume of EUR 150 billion, to support joint defence procurement and the development of the European defence industry. In connection with this instrument, I would like to ask: 1.
What volume of funding from the SAFE instrument does the Commission estimate could realistically be directed to Slovak companies and the Slovak defence industry?

What specific conditions must Slovak firms meet in order to participate fully in projects and consortia financed from the SAFE instrument, for example requirements relating to cooperation, technological standards and security clearances?

What proportion of production and supplies under projects financed by SAFE will have to be carried out in EU Member States, and what proportion may be carried out outside the Union, including in third countries?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) The Commission does not estimate the share of Security Action for Europe (SAFE)1 financing accruing to an individual Member State’s industry, as loans are granted to Member States, not to companies. Slovakia is itself a beneficiary. Moreover, contractors and subcontractors established in Slovakia are eligible to take part in any procurement supported by SAFE, including common procurements conducted by other Member States. The value Slovak undertakings may obtain is therefore not limited to Slovakia’s allocation but depends on their competitiveness across all SAFE supported procurements. Under Article 16 of SAFE, contractors and subcontractors must be established and have their executive management structures located in the EU, the European Economic Area (EEA) – European Free Trade Association (EFTA) or Ukraine, and must not be controlled by a third country, save where guarantees approved by the Member State apply. For defence products related to category two, contractors must also have the ability to decide, without restrictions imposed by third countries, on the definition, adaptation and evolution of the design of the defence product procured, including the legal authority to substitute or remove components subject to such restrictions. These conditions apply uniformly to all participating Member States. The SAFE Regulation does not require any proportion of production to be placed outside the EU. It sets a ceiling: for each end product, the cost of components originating outside the EU, the EEA-EFTA states, and Ukraine may not exceed 35% of the estimated cost of the components. This is a maximum threshold applied per procurement, not a target or a guaranteed share; in practice production takes place predominantly within the EU, the EEAEFTA states and Ukraine.
